entries.name: Karen New Year
entries.capsule: The largest Karen celebration, marking the turn from one rice harvest to the next; Minnesota's date moves.
entries.dateRule: First day of the month KOM spells Pyathoe on the lunar calendar, generally late December or early January. Minnesota organizers announce their gathering each year on a nearby date, which may not match the lunar day. Calendar dates below are the calculated lunar day; organizers' dates are under minnesotaEvents.

dates.source: Calculation found no lunar first day in calendar 2026. KOM's St. Paul gathering for year 2765 was Jan. 1, 2026 (see minnesotaEvents).
Calculated by the seed calendar, not confirmed by an opened page. KOM's St. Paul gathering is Jan. 2 to 3, 2027 (see minnesotaEvents).
Calculated by the seed calendar, not confirmed by an opened page.

entries.whatItMarks: The end of one rice harvest and the start of the next; KOM calls it the largest celebration in the Karen community. Organizers number the years, with 2766 being the January 2027 gathering.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: A large free public gathering in St. Paul, with Karen and U.S. flag salutes, speeches, singing and dance, sports tournaments, a resource fair, games, prizes and a shared meal; recent gatherings were at Washington Technology Magnet School. In January 2010 more than a thousand people came to Roseville Lutheran Church. Greater Minnesota holds its own: Albert Lea at Southwest Middle School (January 2018) and Albert Lea High School (December 2025, several hundred people, with the mayor and superintendent), and Worthington's Karen Community at St. Mary's School on Jan. 1, 2024. No Austin gathering was found.

entries.name: Karen Wrist-Tying Ceremony
entries.capsule: Elders tie string on the wrist so the spirit stays and a person can live free from fear.
entries.dateRule: Held in August, traditionally linked to the August full moon (Karen month Lah Khu, Burmese Wagaung). Minnesota's date is announced each year by organizers. The phrase 'Karen National Wrist-tying Day' did not appear on any page opened.

dates.source: Minnesota ceremony as announced by Karen Culture Organization of Minnesota, listed by KOM
No announcement found
No announcement found

entries.whatItMarks: Calling back a person's spirit and protecting health and belonging. Sources differ on its nature: a Minnesota House document and Drum Publications call it not religious, while the state health toolkit ties it to traditional spirit belief. KOM says monks and elders both take part.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: A weekend in Harris in 2026, with the main ceremony Sunday morning, plus adult soccer, youth volleyball, caneball, a Little Miss Karen pageant, food and booths. People also tie wrists at some weddings, according to KOM.

entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: On Jan. 1, 2024 at St. Mary's School: music, dance, storytelling, food, a song on the Karen harp, and a plaque for the mayor. Buddhists and Christians attended together, with people from Brewster, Round Lake, Fulda and former residents now in Austin. Its vice president said the 2023 gathering was the first in several years.
